topic.title: Can one get good results without having played pokemen before?

messages.content:
Asking for a friend…

Dundertanding the domain of a competition is very often key. Is it true here?

messages.content:
I made it to rank 50 just watching https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eKC5PlYoboE&t=1s and with basic RL principles I learnt from Orbit Wars. So totally possible. Going with a rule based approach probably needs quite a bit of domain knowledge though.

I am however struggling a bit to identify weaknesses at this point, so having domain knowledge or teaming up with someone who does seems important.

messages.content:
I'm in a worse position than your friend since I'm not really familiar with neither Pokemon nor RL literature 😅

As other mentioned, the rules are quite simple and the meta seems to be only a handful of decks so it's quite quick to get familiar with their mechanics. So, my gut feeling tells me that, although very useful, it's not necessary to get a good score as we can get a somewhat decent domain knowledge in a few days.

messages.content: Absolutely! Compared to other trading card games like MTG or Yu-Gi-Oh!, the rules of the Pokémon TCG are much simpler. It's designed so that even a 10-year-old can play it. Of course, just because the rules are simple doesn't necessarily mean it'll be an easy AI task to solve, though!

messages.content: I had never played Pokémon TCG before at all — I’ve only played Hearthstone and Magic: The Gathering. When the competition started, I spent a whole day learning the basic rules, then went offline to a Pokémon gym to find experienced players and picked up some advanced rules from them. I also got a rough idea of how the mainstream decks match up against each other and what the current meta looks like. The rest I just left to reinforcement learning, just orbit wars taught me, haha.
